Getting out of Fremont is smart anyway since they don't actually own the factory. It's going to be easy for people to claim reopening the factory is a public health crisis. However, this isn't Tyson Foods. Tesla has already done this once in Shanghai and they understand safety. Tweet by @elonmusk

1259224273018859522.a: What I mean by Tyson not understanding safety is this: They are only now mandating PPE for employees in the factory in a pandemic? These are meat processing plants. You're telling me PPE isn't already mandatory? Fremont is a ghost town compared to a meatpacking plant.

1259225551707013120.a: There are plenty of factories open here in Indy, for example. Those companies run by competent engineers instead of MBAs have added hazard pay, adjusted schedules to leave an hour between shifts for lab grade sterilization of the lines. Offered vulnerable employees alternatives.

1259227032300519425.a: Seems like the knee jerk reaction is to assume every situation is identical. This is a big planet and every inch is unique. Reopening now needs oversight and zero tolerance. e.g. You don't get fined for slacking on safety. You lose your license to operate a business for good.

1259227919311921152.a: Not to rant, but I am sure most people don't think about how these pandemics start. Exposing employees to raw meat without full PPE every single day during normal operations from the millions of chickens or hogs or cows processed is exactly how you CREATE this type of pandemic.

1259230211218067461.a: Some may say "It's my constitutional right to run a business!" Corporations aren't meant to have rights. People do not have _any_ right to endanger other people. We know how to stay safe from this. Corps aren't safe because politicians created a fine-as-punishment profit model.

1259232263994302464.a: Do I think every building should reopen? No. e.g. Office buildings do not serve a purpose in 2020. Working face to face is not more productive. Cube farms are highly disruptive to those who want to do real work. Fire dishonest workers instead of hover-momming them to distraction.

1259234614217932804.a: We need to take this opportunity to sit back and look at the technology we have and how we do business. Then fundamentally change. We used to have local co-ops. If working at home is distracting why don't we have shared workspaces a short walk from home?

1259234615535026176.a: Look at existing neighborhoods, form human co-ops within them, and reallocate small properties. Make human life enjoyable, sustainable. I intend to focus what's left of my life on this. There are a small set of root causes to overcome which will cascade society toward healing.

1259235981141688322.a: Grandma never told me what to think. She left books where I would find. I learned much pain and suffering has been the quest to find what we once lost. We were kicked out of the Garden of Eden by our own greed. We lost perspective. We mentally left the garden. It's right here: t.co

1259237841613336577.a: I wish you could see what's in my head. I don't have the answers; you all do. But I think I have the map you've forgotten we made. My thinking is not unique but so many are distracted by survival they cannot communicate it. I hope to communicate better before I leave this place.
